newsitem.title: UK: Nat Power up on NatWest comment, tax hopes.
newsitem.headline: Nat Power up on NatWest comment, tax hopes.

text.p: Shares in National Power Plc rose in a strong electricity sector on Monday, extending last week's gains as analysts at NatWest Securities highlighted the stock's yield attractions, dealers said.

Dealers said electricity stocks as a whole continued to gain from talk that the "windfall" tax on privatised utilities planned by the opposition Labour party would not be as large as previously feared.

Separately recent opinion polls have shown the ruling Conservatives closing the gap in the election campaign. "The windfall tax might not be as big as some had feared and if the Tories scrape back in, all the bets are off," said one market-maker.
National Power shares were up 5-1/2p at 531 by 0908 GMT, after on Friday touching a nine-month intraday high of 538p.
Other electricity stocks also rose with PowerGen Plc up 5p at 633, Southern Electric Plc up 14-1/2p at 435 and Scottish Power Plc up 3-1/2p at 380.
Sources said NatWest highlighted National Power and Royal Sun Alliance Plc, down 3-1/2 at 429-1/2, for their high yield and coupled with prospects for real dividend growth.
Analysts at the brokerage were not immediately available for comment.

In the election campaign, some opinion polls indicated a narrowing in Labour's lead with the latest -- Gallup in the Daily Telegraph -- showing the opposition party's lead cut to 17 percentage points from 23 in its previous poll.

Reports last week suggested Labour leader Tony Blair aimed to raise between three and five billion stg from the windfall tax on privatised utilities, less than Labour finance spokesman Gordon Brown had sought.
